eval.golden.customers.explanation: customer_id is the table's primary key, so every row must carry a value for it.
The comment states one row per customer, so customer_id values cannot repeat.
email is the documented contact channel for a customer, so a missing value breaks downstream comms.
The column holds an email address, and this rule enforces local-part, @ and domain structure.
secondary_contact is another way to reach the customer, so it may hold an email.
The comment names ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 explicitly, which is what the two-letter pattern checks.
A row cannot have been created after now, so a future created_at signals a clock fault.
Duplicate of an earlier entry; the pipeline must collapse it.
Names a column that does not exist on the table.
Leaves end_ts unfilled, so the mapping is incomplete.

eval.golden.orders.explanation: order_id is the order's primary key and is required on every row.
A primary key identifies one row, so order_id values must be distinct.
An order without an owning customer cannot be attributed, so the foreign key must be populated.
customer_id looks like a key column, so its values should be distinct.
order_total is a gross monetary total, and a negative gross total is not a representable value.
The comment names ISO 4217, which is the three-letter code this pattern enforces.
An order cannot be placed later than now, so ordered_at must not lead the clock.
The comment enumerates the four legal states, so any other value is unrecognised.
Dispatch follows placement, so ordered_at must not be later than shipped_at.
Binds both slots to one column, which can never fail and is always wrong.
Names a rule id that is not in the candidate set.

eval.golden.raw_landing.explanation: payload carries the record body, so it should always be populated.

eval.golden.invoices.explanation: invoice_id is the primary key and must be present on every row.
One row per invoice means invoice_id values cannot repeat.
The column is the vendor's billing email, so the address structure must hold for remittance to reach them.
An approved budget is a monetary figure that cannot be negative.
Spend against a budget is also a monetary figure, so the same non-negative floor applies to this second column.
The comment names ISO 4217, which the three-letter pattern enforces.
An invoice cannot be issued later than now, so a future issue date is a clock or entry fault.
due_at is a date on the invoice, so it should not be later than now.
Payment falls due after issue, so the issue timestamp must not follow the due timestamp.

eval.golden.shipments.explanation: shipment_id is the primary key and is required on every row.
A shipment key identifies one consignment, so its values must be distinct.
A shipment cannot have left the warehouse later than now, so dispatch must not lead the clock.
Delivery follows dispatch, so the dispatch timestamp must not be later than the delivery timestamp.
Both columns are timestamps on the same consignment, so either ordering could be checked.
The comment names ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, which the two-letter pattern enforces.
A consignment cannot contain a negative number of parcels, and the column is an integer count.

eval.golden.sensor_readings.explanation: reading_id is the primary key and is required on every row.
One row per reading means the key's values cannot repeat.
A sensor cannot record a sample later than now, so a future timestamp indicates a device clock fault.
Relative humidity is expressed as a percentage, so values outside nought to one hundred are impossible.
humidity_percent is numeric and should not go below zero.
A count of transmission errors cannot be negative.
The column holds the device management URL, so it needs an http or https scheme to be reachable.

eval.golden.employees.explanation: employee_id is the primary key of the record and is always required.
One row per employee means the key's values must be distinct.
A blank work email is as unusable as a null one, so emptiness has to be rejected too.
The column is the primary work email address, so the local-part and domain structure must hold.
manager_note is text written by a manager and may contain an email address.
The column holds a home telephone number, which must be dialable for contact to succeed.
Nobody can have joined later than today, so a future joining date is an entry fault.

eval.golden.wide_events.explanation: event_id is the primary key of the event and is required on every row.
One row per event means the key's values cannot repeat.
An event cannot have occurred later than now, so a future timestamp is a clock fault.
The comment names ISO 4217, which the three-letter pattern enforces.
The column is the operator's contact email, so the address structure must hold.
The comment names ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, which the two-letter pattern enforces.
A settlement gross total is monetary and cannot be negative.
The comment enumerates the four legal states, so anything else is unrecognised.
